meaning: What the asset is, in SecurityInsight's one list for every source: Workstation, Server, Mobile, Network device, IoT, Printer, Database, Storage, Web app, Key vault, Network, Container, Compute, Monitoring, AI, Integration, Backup, Security, Management, User, Guest, Service principal, Managed identity, Public IP; Other when no rule names it, Unknown when the sources say nothing.
servicenow: Optional. A filter or a note -- u_proposed_class still proposes the CMDB class.

required: when known (an empty value is left out)
meaning: The asset's kind within its type, one value: SQL Server, Domain controller, SQL Database, Storage account, Switch, ...; General when no rule names it. A CI with a SQL subtype is where SQL findings (u_si_component = SQL) belong.
servicenow: Optional. Use it to pick the sub-CI (for example a SQL instance) your transform map or a script relates SQL findings to.

meaning: What SecurityInsight asks for, on every row of every record: new, update (an unchanged record has the same u_row_hash), close, reopen, held (change nothing; the why is in u_si_reason) or out_of_scope (the record left the output scope; a vulnerable item closes as Out of scope, never as fixed).
servicenow: Use it in the transform: create, update, close or reopen; a held row changes nothing; out_of_scope closes without a fix.

meaning: The batch this row belongs to: <SecurityInsight run id>:<output>. The staging status table (u_si_staging_status) has a writing row and then a complete, failed or held row with the same id.
servicenow: Not mapped. Import a row only when its batch has a complete row in the staging status table.

required: when known (an empty value is left out)
meaning: The clear marker: the columns (comma separated) whose value SecurityInsight now knows is empty. An empty column that is not listed is unknown. Never on a held row.
servicenow: Transform: clear those fields; keep the value of every other empty field.

required: when known (an empty value is left out)
meaning: Why the row is held or out_of_scope, in plain words. Empty otherwise.
servicenow: work notes

required: when known (an empty value is left out)
meaning: The key this record replaces (a device re-onboarded or merged). The old key gets no row of its own.
servicenow: Transform: find the record by this key and move it to the row's key, instead of creating a new one.

meaning: SecurityInsight's stable key for the CI, kept by its identity ledger across re-imaging and id changes -- the SAME key on the CI rows and on the vulnerability rows. Treat it as an opaque string of up to 400 characters (for example mdedeviceid:..., azureresourceid:..., entraobjectid:..., or a GUID).
servicenow: Coalesce key of the staging row. On the CI: u_si_correlation_id, added as the LAST identifier entry (a tie-breaker after your own rules). On a vulnerable item: how the transform finds the CI.

required: when known (an empty value is left out)
meaning: What kind of thing this is: device, azure-resource or identity.
servicenow: Not mapped. Use it in the transform to choose the class family.

required: when known (an empty value is left out)
meaning: The asset name the finding is on.
servicenow: Not mapped (the CI is resolved from u_si_correlation_id).

required: when known (an empty value is left out)
meaning: The CMDB CI the finding is linked to, when SecurityInsight knows its sys_id (only with direct write); usually empty.
servicenow: cmdb_ci when filled; otherwise the transform resolves the CI from u_si_correlation_id, which is the CI rows' key.

meaning: The finding: the id its source gives it -- a CVE id, a Defender for Cloud assessment key, a Defender security configuration id (scid-...) or a SecurityInsight rule id (IDENTITY-..., an attack path). Unique per asset; up to 100 characters (a longer id is cut and ends in ~ and a hash).
servicenow: vulnerability: a CVE -> sn_vul_nvd_entry by CVE id; any other finding -> a third-party entry (sn_vul_third_party_entry) with this id and u_title as its name. Coalesce on u_source_record_id, else u_si_correlation_id + u_vulnerability.

required: when known (an empty value is left out)
meaning: The severity SecurityInsight reports: Very High, Critical, High, Medium-High, Medium or Low.
servicenow: Optional. Your Vulnerability Response computes its own risk; map only if wanted.

meaning: Open or Closed.
servicenow: state (open / closed; closed with the close reason)

required: when known (an empty value is left out)
meaning: When SecurityInsight first reported the finding (UTC).
servicenow: first_found

required: when known (an empty value is left out)
meaning: When SecurityInsight last reported the finding (UTC).
servicenow: last_found

required: when known (an empty value is left out)
meaning: When the record was closed (UTC); empty while open.
servicenow: Not mapped (closed is driven by u_state).

required: when known (an empty value is left out)
meaning: Why the record was closed. Only Remediated is a fix; Out of scope, Duplicate, AssetRetired and NoLongerMonitored are not.
servicenow: u_si_close_reason, and your close code. Never map a reason other than Remediated to Fixed.

required: when known (an empty value is left out)
meaning: How many complete runs in a row the finding was absent on an asset SecurityInsight saw.
servicenow: u_si_absent_runs (optional)

required: when known (an empty value is left out)
meaning: Who opened the record: SecurityInsight. SecurityInsight only ever closes its own records; a record it never sent is never touched.
servicenow: u_si_source, and the ownership check of your transform

meaning: SecurityInsight's own id of the record. It never changes for one finding on one asset -- also not when the CI key is corrected (a re-key).
servicenow: The best coalesce key of the vulnerable item when present (empty for a new finding in an Import Set push).

required: when known (an empty value is left out)
meaning: When the record last changed (UTC): opened, refreshed, closed, reopened, or an absence counted. In an Import Set push: this run.
servicenow: Not mapped. The delta filter of the data source: WHERE u_changed_at > <last import>.

required: when known (an empty value is left out)
meaning: What kind of finding it is: cve, azure-recommendation (Defender for Cloud), endpoint-recommendation (Defender security configuration), identity, attack-path, exposure or recommendation. Every security recommendation is a vulnerability.
servicenow: Use it in the transform to choose the entry type: cve -> sn_vul_nvd_entry, anything else -> sn_vul_third_party_entry.

required: when known (an empty value is left out)
meaning: The finding's name, as its source names it (for a CVE often empty).
servicenow: The third-party entry's name / short description for a finding that is not a CVE.
example: Machines should have vulnerability findings resolved

required: when known (an empty value is left out)
meaning: The SecurityInsight asset id the finding was reported on (the engine's own id; the CI key is u_si_correlation_id).
servicenow: Not mapped (traceability).

required: when known (an empty value is left out)
meaning: The component the finding concerns: OS, SQL, Network, Hardware, Browser, Office, Application or Other -- one value per finding (an operating-system vulnerability on a SQL Server stays OS).
servicenow: The sub-CI of the vulnerable item: a SQL finding to the SQL sub-CI (for example the cmdb_ci_db_mssql_instance under the server), an OS finding to the server itself.

required: when known (an empty value is left out)
meaning: The ServiceNow sub-CI the finding is linked under: OS, SQL or Other by default (component OS -> OS, SQL -> SQL, everything else -> Other); the buckets and the rules that place a finding are set per install (Settings > ServiceNow > Sub-CI mapping). One value per finding, never blank.
servicenow: Link the vulnerable item under the CI's sub-CI of that name (OS findings, SQL findings, Other findings per CI).

required: when known (an empty value is left out)
meaning: The OS family of the asset the finding is on: Windows, Linux, macOS, iOS, Android, Network OS, Other or Unknown -- one value, never blank (Unknown when no source says which OS it runs).
servicenow: Filter or route by operating system (Windows vs. Linux); not needed to link the item.

required: when known (an empty value is left out)
meaning: Whether the finding is fixed in the monthly patch cycle: In monthly cycle (its fix was released -- or, without one dated update, it was first detected -- within SI_PatchCycle_CatchUpDays, default 30, of the collection), Catch-up (older than 1 month), No fix available or Unknown. One value, never blank.
servicenow: Filter or report by patch cycle; not needed to link the item.

meaning: A fingerprint of the record's content (not of the batch, the run or the action). It changes only when the content changes.
servicenow: Keep it on the record (for example in u_si_row_hash) and skip a row whose hash equals it.

required: when known (an empty value is left out)

meaning: The batch: <SecurityInsight run id>:<output>. The same value is on every data row of the batch (u_si_batch_id) and on both status rows of the batch.
servicenow: Your importer: select the data rows of the batch by this id.

meaning: Which output the batch belongs to: servicenow-ci (configuration items) or servicenow-vulnerable-item (vulnerable items).
servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

meaning: writing (the batch has started), complete (every row was accepted: import it), failed (some rows were not accepted: do not import) or held (stopped before or while sending: do not import); or feedback (information only: the import result SecurityInsight read back for a complete batch -- never a batch state).
servicenow: Your importer: complete = import the batch's rows (u_si_batch_id); failed / held = do not import; writing with no end row after a few hours = the push stopped, do not import.
